results.title: Three Ways Iran War Could End And What It Means For Global Energy - Forbes
results.content:
In the wake of American and Israeli strikes against Iran on February 28th, Tehran reacted swiftly, attacking energy infrastructure, water desalination plants, and other soft targets across the Middle East as well as moving to close the Strait of Hormuz. Closure of the vital Strait has long been foreseen by security experts, including this author, who warned about the Iranian regime’s intentions in a 2007 Congressional testimony, but it still shocked markets. Crude oil prices jumped from approximately $70 dollars a barrel to just over $110 a barrel as the crisis entered its second month. [...] If Iran is decisively defeated, oil prices are likely to fall as supply returns to global markets and the Strait fully reopens, with the world returning to business as usual by Q326-Q426. The U.S. will maintain its role as a rule-setter not just in the Middle East but also in upholding freedom of navigation, keeping global trade routes open.

As the early communist Russian leader Leon Trotsky famously declared, "War, comrades, is a great locomotive of history." Regardless of how this war ends, the crisis will have a lasting impact on global energy markets, economic growth, and international security, and the strategic shifts it triggers will endure for years and decades.
